title: fix(auto-reply): keep memory flush alive before adoption
body:
Closes #137294

## What Problem This Solves

A required preflight memory flush can legitimately run longer than the shorter channel-ingress claim-to-adoption watchdog. Before compaction starts its existing heartbeat, the watchdog can abort and replay the message, restarting the same maintenance work.

## Why This Change Was Made

This reshapes the PR around the lifecycle already shipped by #150040 instead of introducing a second timeout owner. A runnable memory flush now starts the existing pre-adoption lifecycle heartbeat immediately before its bounded run context and stops it in the same cleanup path.

Skipped memory flushes do not start a heartbeat, so unrelated preparation stalls remain covered by the ingress watchdog. Compaction continues to use the same lifecycle helper. There is no new configuration, environment variable, public callback, or storage schema.

The existing prompt-token estimator now lives in `memory-flush.ts` and keeps the normalization `main` already uses. Production delta on this rebase is +18/-10.

## User Impact

Long, healthy memory checkpoints can finish without the ingress layer aborting and replaying the message. Turns that never enter bounded maintenance still retain the normal stall timeout and retry behavior.

## Evidence

Head: `44261581e0b1a1c9462cf1eeb2f451131a8ab3f2` (rebased onto current `main`; previous head `fa87f25a85a746a884434b757ca570e461808f70`)

- Runner proof on this head: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-direct-runtime-config.test.ts` passed 22/22, including the runnable and skipped memory-flush heartbeat cases.
- Changed-file gate on this head: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` exited 0.
- Real-ingress proof recorded on the previous head `fa87f25a85a746a884434b757ca570e461808f70`: an isolated Linux/Node 24 Gateway used Telegram `getUpdates` polling with a synthetic account, workspace, state directory, and local mock provider. A required pre-reply memory flush was held for 35,000 ms while the ingress watchdog was 10,000 ms. That trace recorded 2 delivered updates, 2 inbound runs, 2 final deliveries, `finalAfterFlush=true`, and `handlerTimeout=false`; no update was replayed. This rebase keeps that same heartbeat placement.
- Exact trace summary: `{"head":"fa87f25a85a746a884434b757ca570e461808f70","transport":"Telegram getUpdates","watchdogMs":10000,"memoryFlushHoldMs":35000,"memoryFlushRequests":2,"totalProviderResponsesRequests":5,"updateDeliveries":2,"finalDeliveries":2,"inboundRuns":2,"finalAfterFlush":true,"handlerTimeout":false}`.
- Stored-data compatibility: there is no persistent data-model or vector/embedding metadata change. The estimator move changes no stored field, serialization format, migration, or upgrade path.

Related: #150040


## Maintainer verification

[Current-main baseline, exact-head Gateway proof, quick-flush controls, and failing-before/passing-after regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137359#issuecomment-5928842621).

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes. Contributor commits and credit are unchanged.
